text:
alina: Heads-up: planning to enable halley-lite-13b-v1 in catalog during the 16:00 PT change window. Initial canary: us-east-1 8%, eu-central-1 4%. Fallback order proposed: halley-13b-v0 -> halley-lite-quant -> halley-mini. Any blockers?

deploy-bot: scheduled catalog enable for halley-lite-13b-v1 at 2024-08-02T16:00:00-07:00. Canary split us-east-1=8%, eu-central-1=4%. Auto-rollback: p99>1.8x or error rate >0.5% over 10m.

rob: ack. i'll kick off the regression harness against us-east canary once traffic lands.

dave: added a small safety eval set (halley-regen-smoke) and mem+gpu probe. will post mem trends.

alina: also note: quant fallback is intentionally lower priority because previous test showed larger memory variance. keeping that order unless we see capacity issues.

ci-bot: preflight checks: model artifact sha ok, container image passed scan, infra quota checked. All green.

deploy-bot: deploy logs:
```
[16:00:02] deploy: register halley-lite-13b-v1 canary
[16:00:18] nodes provisioned: serve-a12, serve-a13
[16:00:47] model cached and warmed
[16:01:10] traffic shifted: us-east-1=8%
[16:01:35] eu-central-1=4%
```

infra-bot: metric alarm: us-east-1 mem_rss increased 1.9x vs baseline at 16:06:42 - alert HALLEY-MEM-20240802-160642.

dave: seeing mem RSS climb on a subset of long-context generation tests. OOM not hit but GC thrash visible. running heap snapshots now.

rob: smoke tests show increased tail latency too, but error rate still low. I recommend throttling EU immediately and reducing US canary to 2% while we inspect.

alina: agree. reduce us-east to 2% and set eu to pinned v0 for safety. we don't want user traffic impacted.

deploy-bot: executing scale commands: `deploy scale --region us-east-1 --model halley-lite-13b-v1 --percent 2`

deploy-bot: executing pin: `deploy pin --region eu-central-1 --model halley-13b-v0 --reason "memory tail spike on v1 canary"`

deploy-bot: result: us-east-1=2% active, eu-central-1 pinned->halley-13b-v0 (v1 draining).

ci-bot: running quick canary tests on remaining us-east nodes.

dave: heap snapshots uploaded -> https://internal/diag/halley/20240802/heap-xyz (link). early look: memory amplification in tokenizer cache on longer prompts. suspect new tokenizer change in v1.

rob: if tokenizer cache is the cause, we can flip a runtime flag to limit cache size for v1 nodes. can someone make a toggle?

alina: chime in: make it a per-model runtime toggle and roll it in a hotfix. prefer not to rollback the artifact until we confirm.

dave: started branch `runtime/limit/token-cache` PR #9001. adding a small integ test.

deploy-bot: note: auto-rollback remains enabled for us-east canary with thresholds. manual pin applied in EU.

infra-bot: scheduled monitor window 16:05-18:05 PT. paging list: eng-releases@redwood.com, infra@redwood.com.

ci-bot: test results so far: regen-smoke passed 93/100 on us-east at 2% traffic, failed cases correlate with >5k token prompts.

rob: let's hold public release notes until we know root cause. internal changelog draft for catalog: "halley-lite-13b-v1: improved throughput and summarization quality for medium contexts. Canary launched 2024-08-02; EU canary pinned to previous stable due to memory amplification on long contexts; mitigation in progress."

alina: action items:
- dave: finish heap analysis and confirm tokenizer cache hypothesis (ETA 45m)
- devops: review and approve PR #9001 and prepare hotfix rollout (ETA 60m)
- rob: re-run regression suite after hotfix on us-east at 2% (ETA after hotfix)

rob: PR #9001 looks good, adding +1.

deploy-bot: when hotfix merges, plan: patch runtime on v1 canary nodes in us-east, ramp to 10% over 30m with p99 guardrail 1.5x. EU to be re-evaluated after 2h stable telemetry.

alina: ok. i'll coordinate the restart once we have a passing canary post-hotfix. reconvene in 1h or earlier if anything changes. :calendar:

ci-bot: final note: we should include the per-model cache toggle as part of catalog metadata so teams can opt-in without full artifact rollbacks. filing ticket INFRA-3212.
